title: Clear Your Debts: How 12 Month Consolidation Works
author: freyawilson
contentHtml:
Debt consolidation seems to be the best solution when you are juggling repayments of multiple debts. You take out a personal loan to pay off all your existing debts once and for all, so you are left with only one large loan to pay off. However, it is crucial to note that these loans are consolidated only to discharge short-term high-cost debts. On no account can consolidation loans be used to club large loans such as mortgages, auto loans, and other instalment loans. 

If you have credit card debt, instead of personal loans, you will have to apply for a sufficient budget. They come with an introductory period, not more than 24 months, and if you manage to settle the debt within that period, no interest will be charged. If it expires, you will have to discharge the whole amount of the debt.  

How does 12-month consolidation work? 

First off, you need to understand that consolidation is nothing but taking out a new loan to discharge your existing debts once and for all. This enables you to spread the cost of the debt over a number of months. Interest rates remain fixed throughout the repayment term.  

It is essential to understand that consolidation does not reduce your debt amount. It only spreads the cost of the debt. Consolidation results in a change in structure, interest rates, and the number of payments.  

There is no guarantee that the total cost of consolidation will be lower than the total cost of managing all loans separately. Lower interest rates are generally available for good credit borrowers. However, a stellar credit rating does not guarantee it. The total cost of a consolidation loan varies by interest rates and repayment terms. Getting bad credit debt consolidation loans could be challenging to qualify. Most lenders restrict a large loan amount for subprime borrowers.  

Work out what you currently owe 

Before comparing, you should get a complete picture of your existing debts. First off, you need to figure out how much debt you owe. Check the APR of each loan you owe, and monthly payments. Do not forget to include early repayment charges.  

Add up the total amount of existing loans. This is the minimum amount that you need to borrow to pay them off once and for all. Now add up the monthly payments because this is a baseline figure to compare the cost of a personal finance.  

At the time of consolidating your loans, you should compare the total cost and monthly payments. Most of the time, consolidation seems to be the best alternative because they merge loans into a lump-sum payment. Since they spread the cost of the debt, they tend to be more affordable, but choosing a longer repayment term will increase total interest payments.  

Before consolidation, you should consider the following questions: 

  • What interest rates are you paying currently?  
  • Will consolidation help with lowering interest payments? 
  • Are there any early repayment charges? 
  • What will be the size of monthly payments after consolidation? Is it higher or lower than the current monthly payment? 

 Decide whether consolidation is right for you 

Consolidation is not an ideal option for everyone. You need to examine whether this eases the burden of payments carefully. Will you be able to get out of debt sooner? It is worth remembering that consolidation loans cannot help you if you are struggling with minimum monthly repayments, and if your existing debts are less expensive than the cost of a new personal loan. 

It is essential to note that lenders will carefully analyse your repayment capacity at the time of approving a personal finance. It is highly unlikely that lenders will be able to consolidate all your existing short-term high-cost debts. Some lenders do not even lend more than £1,000, which means you will still have to handle some loans separately.  

Check your credit score and eligibility 

You should check your credit score before applying for a consolidation loan. Lenders will peruse your credit history, which is a part of your application. It is crucial to understand that your credit history should be strong. Even if you are struggling with debt payments, try to apply for a consolidation before missing a payment. If your credit history is not up to scratch, you will most likely be refused. Some lenders might be willing to accept your application, but they will charge very high interest rates.  

Try to get a copy of your credit report from all credit reference agencies. You can get a free copy from them once a year. Make sure that your credit report is accurate. It should not consist of any unidentified accounts. Sometimes, inaccurate information leads to a poor credit score. This may cause difficulties while getting approval for a loan.  

Compare consolidation options 

You should compare interest rates, APRs, repayment terms and the total cost. This comparison will help you understand whether it is cheaper than existing loans. You should compare personal loan rates from different lenders.   

Apply for a consolidation loan 

Once you have picked a lender, you should fill out the application form. Most lenders will require personal details, your employment status, income information and debts you want to consolidate. They will require your bank statement to ensure you will not struggle with payments. It depends on them whether or not they want to approve your application.  

Manage your single monthly payments 

Once you have got a loan approved, you should clear all your existing debts and start making monthly payments on a new personal loan.  

The bottom line 

At the time of taking out a consolidation loan, you should carefully analyse whether it will help you save money on interest. A golden rule of thumb says that you should have a good credit score while consolidating your debts. Make sure that you do not borrow more than the amount of existing debts, and use your credit cards with caution. Consolidation cannot help you stop getting into debt unless you change your habits.
